reason: Prior measurements show no promoted layout or scheduling variant, and the noisy scores do not identify a bottleneck. I rank the one-call traversal experiments first: they target reuse without adding SME entries, though their pointer remapping has correctness risk. B-panel packing and prefetching are narrower but add timed work with no evidence it will pay off. Transpose fusion and the general-fallback transpose change are larger or do not target n=512. The panel64 proposal needs a helper that is not supplied. The two K-loop proposals assume a two-K body absent from the current source evidence. Alignment has no reported failure or speed hypothesis, so it ranks last.
